cover.title: Homes Cost Nearly 5 Years Of Pay
cover.label: MEDIAN HOME

lines.text: The typical US home costs nearly five years of household income.
lines.say: The typical US home costs nearly five years of household income.

lines.text: In the 1990s, it was about three. So what happened?
lines.say: In the nineteen nineties, it was about three. So what happened?

lines.text: NAR's median existing-home price hit a record $414,400 in 2025, up from $346,900 in 2021.
lines.say: The median existing home hit a record four hundred fourteen thousand dollars in twenty twenty-five, up from about three forty-seven thousand in twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: Harvard found existing-home prices up 54% since 2020.
lines.say: Harvard found existing-home prices up fifty-four percent since twenty twenty.

lines.text: Reason one: not enough homes. Freddie Mac estimated a shortage of about 3.7 million in 2024.
lines.say: Reason one: not enough homes. Freddie Mac estimated a shortage of about three point seven million in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Reason two: rates, which raise the monthly cost. The average 30-year rate was 7.03% on Sept. 24, 2026.
lines.say: Reason two: rates, which raise the monthly cost. The average thirty-year rate was about seven percent in late September.

lines.text: With 10% down on August 2026's $429,100 median, that's about $2,577 a month at 7.03%, versus about $1,628 at 3%.
lines.say: With ten percent down on August's median home, that's about twenty-five hundred seventy-seven dollars a month. At three percent, it'd be about sixteen hundred thirty.

lines.text: Reason three: owners with cheap old mortgages stay put, so fewer homes get listed.
lines.say: Reason three: owners with cheap old mortgages stay put, so fewer homes get listed.

lines.text: Short supply, high rates, few sellers: that's the wall buyers hit.

post.title: Why the typical home costs nearly 5 years of income
post.ig:
The typical US home costs nearly five years of household income.
Harvard JCHS: price-to-income was 4.7 in 2025, vs about 3.2 in the 1990s; existing-home prices up 54% since 2020.
NAR median existing-home price: $346,900 in 2021, a record $414,400 in 2025.
Why: a shortage Freddie Mac put at ~3.7M homes (2024), 30-year rates at 7.03% (Sept 24, 2026), and owners locked into cheap old mortgages.
Example: 10% down on Aug 2026's $429,100 median = ~$2,577/mo at 7.03% vs ~$1,628 at 3%.
Sources: Harvard JCHS 2026; NAR; Freddie Mac.
News and education, not financial advice.
